notes: Read all 52 source lines (numbered) before editing. The module is a single non-visual utility: safeRandomUUID() returns an RFC 4122 v4 UUID. No JSX, no Recharts/Leaflet, no web UI components, no imports — the only browser-coupled surface is the `crypto` global (crypto.randomUUID + crypto.getRandomValues), already guarded defensively on web with `typeof crypto !== 'undefined'` and a Math.random last resort.

L1-17 the function JSDoc (v4 even when crypto.randomUUID is unavailable; secure-context restriction; LAN-IP/plain-HTTP undefined-randomUUID rationale; getRandomValues available since 2011; the Math.random last-resort + not-cryptographically-secure caveat + the uniqueness-only acceptable-use note) is ported verbatim above safeRandomUUID, with one added clause naming 'a pure React Native runtime with no Web Crypto polyfill' as another way the Math.random branch is reached. A leading // file header additionally documents the single browser-only substitution (the globalThis.crypto probe).
L18 `export function safeRandomUUID(): string {` ported verbatim (same name, no args, string return).

L19-25 first try block (`if (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && typeof crypto.randomUUID === 'function') return crypto.randomUUID()` with the empty catch carrying the `/* ITP / locked iframe — drop through to the constructed-UUID branch */` comment): the two `typeof crypto !== 'undefined'` existence checks are replaced by a single `const webCrypto = getWebCrypto()` probe at the top of the function (the getWebStorage / resolveAudioContextCtor globalThis-probe precedent), because the native tsconfig omits the DOM lib so the bare `crypto` identifier is undeclared and `typeof crypto` would not compile. The guard becomes `if (webCrypto && typeof webCrypto.randomUUID === 'function') return webCrypto.randomUUID()`. The property access (.randomUUID) and the call stay inside the try, exactly as on web, so the ITP/locked-iframe throw is still caught; the comment is preserved byte-for-byte. Acquiring the crypto reference via globalThis.crypto is the safe analogue of `typeof crypto` and never throws.
L27 `const bytes = new Uint8Array(16)` ported verbatim (Uint8Array is core es5/es2015, available under the native es2019 lib; no DOM dependency).

L28-36 second try block: `if (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && typeof crypto.getRandomValues === 'function') crypto.getRandomValues(bytes)` -> `if (webCrypto && typeof webCrypto.getRandomValues === 'function') webCrypto.getRandomValues(bytes)`; the `else { for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) bytes[i] = Math.floor(Math.random() * 256) }` branch and the catch-fallback `for` loop are ported byte-for-byte (single-line braceless for matches the recentPages/notificationSound house style). Same three outcomes: real getRandomValues seeds the bytes; missing crypto -> Math.random seed; any throw -> Math.random seed.

L38-41 the RFC 4122 §4.4 comment and the two version/variant byte ops (`bytes[6] = (bytes[6] & 0x0f) | 0x40` and `bytes[8] = (bytes[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80`) ported verbatim — bitwise operators are unrestricted by the @react-native eslint config (validateImport.ts uses the same `& 0x3f` / `<<` / `>>` ops and passes lint).

L43-44 `const hex: string[] = []` then `for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) hex.push(bytes[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'))` ported verbatim (padStart is es2017.string, transitively included by the native es2019 lib).
L45-51 the return template assembling the 8-4-4-4-12 hyphenated UUID string from hex[0..15] is ported character-for-character (same group boundaries, same backtick segments joined with `+`).
L52 closing brace + trailing newline preserved.

Added native-only artifacts with no web equivalent: the `WebCryptoLike` structural interface (randomUUID?: () => string; getRandomValues?: <T extends Uint8Array>(array: T) => T) describing exactly the two members used, and `getWebCrypto()` which returns the globalThis.crypto object when it is a non-null object else undefined — the established getWebStorage probe shape. These exist solely to reach the crypto global in a DOM-lib-free, typecheck-clean way; they do not alter behaviour.

Additive native-only export `nativeSafeUUIDCapabilities` ({cryptoRandomUUIDAvailable:false, cryptoGetRandomValuesAvailable:false} as const) documents the explicit native-unavailable state per the conversion contract (mirrors nativeNotificationSoundCapabilities); react-native-web or a Web Crypto polyfill may still light the real APIs up at runtime via the probe, and even without them safeRandomUUID still returns a valid v4 UUID via the Math.random fallback the web source already documents.
